org-lsp.server.path.markdownDescription: Path to the `org-lsp` server binary. When empty, the binary bundled with the extension is used, or else `org-lsp` from `PATH`.

org-lsp.conceal.markdownDescription: Hide what Org hides: link brackets and targets (`linkDescriptive`), and emphasis markers with `hideEmphasisMarkers`. It shows on the lines with a cursor.

org-lsp.images.markdownDescription: Show images in place of links to image files and of LaTeX fragments (`C-c C-x C-v`, `C-c C-x C-l`; `#+STARTUP: inlineimages`, `latexpreview`). VS Code cannot leave lines free for an image: an image takes the height of a line, and shows whole on hover. LaTeX previews need Emacs, `latex` and `dvipng`.

org-lsp.latexForeground.markdownDescription: The color LaTeX previews are drawn in, such as `#d4d4d4`. When empty, black on a light theme and light gray on a dark one.

enumDescriptions: As notifications, in the corner of the window.
In the status bar for a few seconds, as Emacs's echo area shows them.
org-lsp.messages.markdownDescription: How Org's messages show (`Priority of current item set to A`, `Effort is now 1:00`). Errors always show as notifications.

enumDescriptions: In an editor group below the current one.

org-lsp.winSplitMode.markdownDescription: Where the agenda and capture buffers open.

enumDescriptions: Emacs's keys: `Ctrl+C Ctrl+T`, `Tab`, `Shift+arrows`, … in Org files, and Org's single letters in the agenda. `Ctrl+C` then waits for a second key in Org files instead of copying (`Ctrl+Insert` still copies).

The Neovim plugin's keys, for VSCodeVim: those VS Code can bind without taking keys from Vim (`Tab`, `Ctrl+Space`, `Ctrl+A`, …) in Normal mode, and the agenda's. docs/keys/vscode.org shows how to add the leader keys to VSCodeVim.
No keys: bind the commands yourself in keybindings.json.
org-lsp.keys.markdownDescription: Which keys the extension binds in Org files, the agenda, the date prompt and capture buffers.

org-lsp.settings.markdownDescription: The server's options, for example `{ "agendaFiles": ["~/org"], "todoKeywords": ["TODO", "NEXT", "|", "DONE"], "logDone": "time" }`. Without `agendaFiles`, the agenda is built from the Org files in the workspace folders. The options and their defaults are listed in [docs/configuration.org](https://github.com/kristijanhusak/org-lsp/blob/main/docs/configuration.org).

config_file.markdownDescription: The shared configuration file, whose options this editor's go on top of: `false` for none, or the path of another file (JSON if it ends in `.json`, else TOML). Unset, it is `$ORG_LSP_CONFIG`, else `config.toml` or `config.json` in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/org-lsp` (`~/.config/org-lsp`; `%APPDATA%\org-lsp` on Windows).

org_agenda_files.markdownDescription: Files, directories and glob patterns (`*`, `?`, `**`) the agenda is built from. `~/` is the home directory, and a directory stands for the Org files directly in it. When empty, the agenda is built from the Org files under the workspace folders (hidden directories, `node_modules` and `target` left out), or else from the Org files that are open. (`org-agenda-files`)

org_todo_keywords.markdownDescription: The TODO sequence, written like Org's `#+TODO:` line. `|` separates the states that count as done; without it the last keyword is the only done state. `TODO(t)` gives a keyword a key for fast selection, and `WAIT(w@/!)` makes it log a note (`@`) or the time (`!`) on entering and leaving it. Several sequences go in a list of lists, `[["TODO", "|", "DONE"], ["REPORT", "|", "FIXED"]]`; cycling stays in the sequence of the entry, and `C-S-<right>` switches to the next. A list that starts with `type` is a type sequence (`#+TYP_TODO:`): each of its keywords goes straight to done. A file's own `#+TODO:` lines take precedence. (`org-todo-keywords`)

org_todo_keyword_faces.markdownDescription: Faces for particular TODO keywords: a color, `{ "WAIT": "orange" }`, or attributes written as Org writes them, `{ "CANCELLED": ":foreground gray :slant italic :strike-through t" }` (`:foreground`, `:background`, `:weight bold`, `:slant italic`, `:underline t`, `:strike-through t`). Shown in Org files and in the agenda by Neovim, Vim and VS Code. (`org-todo-keyword-faces`)

org_priority_faces.markdownDescription: Faces for particular priorities, by their letter, written as in `org_todo_keyword_faces`: `{ "A": ":foreground red :weight bold" }`. (`org-priority-faces`)

org_tag_faces.markdownDescription: Faces for particular tags of headlines, written as in `org_todo_keyword_faces`: `{ "work": "orange" }`. Shown in Org files (not the agenda, as in Emacs) by Neovim, Vim and VS Code. (`org-tag-faces`)

org_log_done.markdownDescription: Write `CLOSED:` with the time when an entry is done, and with `note` ask for a note too. A file's `#+STARTUP:` words `logdone`, `lognotedone` and `nologdone` change it there; an entry's `LOGGING` property (inherited) says what its state changes log instead: those words, `logrepeat` and its relatives, and keywords with what they log (`WAIT(@/!)`), or `nil` for nothing. (`org-log-done`)

org_log_repeat.markdownDescription: Record when a repeating entry is done and moves to its next date. `#+STARTUP:` `logrepeat`, `lognoterepeat` and `nologrepeat` change it in a file, and the `LOGGING` property in an entry. (`org-log-repeat`)

org_M_RET_may_split_line.markdownDescription: Inserting a heading, an item or a table row (M-RET) in the middle of a line splits it, the rest going to the new one; `false`: it goes in after the line. One by context: `{ "headline": false, "item": true, "table": true }`, `default` for those not named. (`org-M-RET-may-split-line`)

org_blank_before_new_entry.markdownDescription: Whether a new heading (`heading`) and a new item (`plain_list_item`) get an empty line before them: `true`, `false`, or `"auto"`, as the headings or items around them have. (`org-blank-before-new-entry`)

org_insert_heading_respect_content.markdownDescription: M-RET and M-S-RET outside lists put the new heading after the subtree, as C-RET does. (`org-insert-heading-respect-content`)

org_special_ctrl_a_e.markdownDescription: How C-a and C-e (`org.beginning.of.line`, `org.end.of.line`) move on a headline or an item: `true` to the start of the headline's title, after the stars, TODO keyword and priority, or after the item's bullet and check-box, and to the end of the title, before the tags; the same key again to the line's own start or end. `reversed` goes to the line's start or end first, and to those places on the same key right after. A pair, as `[true, false]`, sets C-a and C-e apart. With `false` the key keeps the editor's own meaning. (`org-special-ctrl-a/e`)

org_special_ctrl_k.markdownDescription: C-k (`org.kill.line`) on a headline kills the text to the tags, and the tags when the cursor is past the title; at the start of the line, the whole line. With `false` the key keeps the editor's own meaning. (`org-special-ctrl-k`)

org_list_two_spaces_after_bullet_regexp.markdownDescription: An Emacs regexp: the bullets it matches get two spaces after them when Org writes them (a new item, a bullet changed, a list repaired). (`org-list-two-spaces-after-bullet-regexp`)

org_list_demote_modify_bullet.markdownDescription: By bullet (`-`, `+`, `*`, `1.`, `1)`), the bullet an item gets when it is indented: `{ "+": "-", "-": "+" }`. (`org-list-demote-modify-bullet`)

org_list_indent_offset.markdownDescription: How many more columns sub-items are indented, past their parent's bullet. (`org-list-indent-offset`)

org_list_automatic_rules.markdownDescription: `checkbox`: the statistics cookies are counted again when a box changes, and colored as done or not. `indent`: indenting the first item of a list with its children (M-S-<right>) moves the whole list. A rule left out of the object is off. (`org-list-automatic-rules`)

org_checkbox_hierarchical_statistics.markdownDescription: A checkbox cookie counts the boxes of the items right below it; `false` counts every box further down too, as `recursive` in a `COOKIE_DATA` property does. (`org-checkbox-hierarchical-statistics`)

org_table_number_regexp.markdownDescription: An Emacs regexp: the fields it matches are numbers, and a column mostly of numbers aligns right. (`org-table-number-regexp`)

org_table_number_fraction.markdownDescription: How much of a column's filled fields must be numbers for it to align right. (`org-table-number-fraction`)

org_table_automatic_realign.markdownDescription: TAB and RET in a table align it before they move; `false`: only C-c C-c and the commands that change rows or columns do. (`org-table-automatic-realign`)

org_table_tab_jumps_over_hlines.markdownDescription: TAB at the end of a row before a horizontal line goes to the row after it; `false`: it makes a row before the line. (`org-table-tab-jumps-over-hlines`)

org_table_shrunk_column_indicator.markdownDescription: What shows at the end of each field of a shrunk column. (`org-table-shrunk-column-indicator`)

org_table_formula_constants.markdownDescription: Constants for the table formulas of every file, by name: `{ "c": "299792458." }` gives `$c`. A file's `#+CONSTANTS:` come first. (`org-table-formula-constants`)

org_table_relative_ref_may_cross_hline.markdownDescription: Whether a relative reference in a formula (`@-1`) goes past a horizontal line: `false` stops at the field next to it, `"error"` makes the formula fail. (`org-table-relative-ref-may-cross-hline`)

org_table_formula_create_columns.markdownDescription: A field formula past the last column adds the columns it needs, rather than failing. (`org-table-formula-create-columns`)

org_table_duration_custom_format.markdownDescription: How a formula with `;t` writes a duration: a number of seconds, minutes, hours or days, or hours and minutes. (`org-table-duration-custom-format`)

org_table_duration_hour_zero_padding.markdownDescription: Durations of formulas (`;T`, `;U`) have their hours on two digits: `08:32:34` rather than `8:32:34`. (`org-table-duration-hour-zero-padding`)

org_calc_default_modes.markdownDescription: The modes table formulas start with: `float_format`, `["float", digits]`, `["fix", decimals]` or `["sci", digits]`, and `angle_mode`, `"deg"` or `"rad"`. A formula's own modes (`;f2`) win; Calc's other modes are not offered. (`org-calc-default-modes`)

org_table_formula_evaluate_inline.markdownDescription: TAB and RET on a field that is a formula (`=$1*2`, `:=...`) evaluate it, which org-lsp refuses (the formula goes in a `#+TBLFM:` line); `false` leaves the field as text. (`org-table-formula-evaluate-inline`)

org_table_allow_automatic_line_recalcula.markdownDescription: TAB, RET and C-c C-c on a line marked `#` recalculate it. (`org-table-allow-automatic-line-recalculation`)

org_list_use_circular_motion.markdownDescription: Moving to the next item from the last goes to the first, and back; moving the last item down puts it first, the first up puts it last. (`org-list-use-circular-motion`)

org_enforce_todo_dependencies.markdownDescription: An entry cannot be done while a child is not, or, under a parent with the `ORDERED` property, while an earlier sibling is not: the change is refused with what blocks it. (`org-enforce-todo-dependencies`)

org_agenda_dim_blocked_tasks.markdownDescription: Dim the tasks of the agenda and the TODO list that their dependencies keep from being done (with `org_enforce_todo_dependencies` or `org_enforce_todo_checkbox_dependencies`); `invisible` leaves them out instead, except those blocked by checkboxes, which stay dimmed. (`org-agenda-dim-blocked-tasks`)

org_enforce_todo_checkbox_dependencies.markdownDescription: An entry cannot be done while it has an unchecked box. (`org-enforce-todo-checkbox-dependencies`)

org_log_refile.markdownDescription: Record when an entry is refiled (`Refiled on [2026-05-18 Mon 10:30]`), with `note` asking for a note too. `#+STARTUP:` `logrefile`, `lognoterefile` and `nologrefile` change it in the file refiled to. (`org-log-refile`)

org_log_reschedule.markdownDescription: Record when a scheduled date changes or is removed (`Rescheduled from "[2026-05-18 Mon]" on …`), with `note` asking for a note too. `#+STARTUP:` `logreschedule`, `lognotereschedule` and `nologreschedule` change it in a file. (`org-log-reschedule`)

org_log_redeadline.markdownDescription: Record when a deadline changes or is removed (`New deadline from …`), with `note` asking for a note too. `#+STARTUP:` `logredeadline`, `lognoteredeadline` and `nologredeadline` change it in a file. (`org-log-redeadline`)

org_log_into_drawer.markdownDescription: Put state changes and notes into a drawer: `true` for `LOGBOOK`, or the name of a drawer. `#+STARTUP:` `logdrawer` and `nologdrawer` change it in a file; an entry's `LOG_INTO_DRAWER` property (inherited) says which drawer for it (`t` for `LOGBOOK`, `nil` for none). (`org-log-into-drawer`)

org_log_done_with_time.markdownDescription: The `CLOSED:` timestamp of an entry done has the time, not only the date. (`org-log-done-with-time`)

org_log_note_headings.markdownDescription: The heading of each kind of note, by kind: `done` (`CLOSING NOTE %t`), `state` (`State %-12s from %-12S %t`), `note`, `reschedule`, `delschedule`, `redeadline`, `deldeadline`, `refile` and `clock_out`. In a heading `%t` is the time, `%T` the time active, `%d` and `%D` the date, `%s` the new state or date and `%S` the old one, `%u` the login name and `%U` the full name; an empty heading leaves the note its text only. Kinds left out keep Org's headings. Habits take notes with the `done` heading for days done. (`org-log-note-headings`)

org_log_states_order_reversed.markdownDescription: Put a new state note, note or clock line above the others (`false`: below them). `#+STARTUP:` `logstatesreversed` and `nologstatesreversed` change it in a file. (`org-log-states-order-reversed`)

org_log_state_notes_insert_after_drawers.markdownDescription: Without a log drawer, put notes after the drawers right under the headline and planning line, not before them. (`org-log-state-notes-insert-after-drawers`)

org_log_note_clock_out.markdownDescription: Ask for a note when the clock stops (`org.clock.out`), which goes right after the clock line. `#+STARTUP:` `lognoteclock-out` and `nolognoteclock-out` change it in a file. (`org-log-note-clock-out`)

org_provide_todo_statistics.markdownDescription: Update the `[1/3]` and `[33%]` cookies of the parent when a state changes, counting the entries with a keyword (`true`), every entry (`all-headlines`, those without a keyword as not done), those with these keywords and the done ones (a list), or those of the first list as not done and of the second as done (two lists). `false` leaves the cookies. (`org-provide-todo-statistics`)

org_hierarchical_todo_statistics.markdownDescription: TODO statistics count the children only; `false`: the whole subtree, and the cookies above too. A `COOKIE_DATA` property with `recursive` does this for a subtree. (`org-hierarchical-todo-statistics`)

org_closed_keep_when_no_todo.markdownDescription: Keep the `CLOSED:` timestamp when an entry is left with no keyword. (`org-closed-keep-when-no-todo`)

org_todo_state_tags_triggers.markdownDescription: Tags that change with the state, by state: a keyword, `""` for none, `todo` for any not done, `done` for any done; each a list of tags to set (`+TAG`) or remove (`-TAG`), in order: `{ "WAIT": ["+waiting"], "todo": ["-done"], "done": ["+done", "-waiting"] }`. (`org-todo-state-tags-triggers`)

org_tags_column.markdownDescription: Where tags are aligned after a change to a headline. Negative: they end at that column. (`org-tags-column`)

org_use_tag_inheritance.markdownDescription: Which tags entries inherit from their parents and from `#+FILETAGS:`: `true` for all, `false` for none, a list of tags, or a regexp (Emacs syntax) tags must match. Inherited tags count in tag searches and show in the agenda. (`org-use-tag-inheritance`)

org_tags_exclude_from_inheritance.markdownDescription: Tags never inherited, when `org_use_tag_inheritance` is `true` or a regexp. (`org-tags-exclude-from-inheritance`)

org_use_property_inheritance.markdownDescription: Which properties an entry without them takes from its parents, the file's property drawer and `#+PROPERTY:` lines, in property searches (`OWNER="alice"`): `true` for all, `false` for none, a list of names, or a regexp (Emacs syntax). `CATEGORY` and `ARCHIVE` are always inherited. (`org-use-property-inheritance`)

org_global_properties.markdownDescription: Properties every entry inherits, after those of `#+PROPERTY:` lines: chiefly the allowed values of a property, which setting it offers and `S-<right>` and `S-<left>` go through on its line (`{ "Effort_ALL": "0:10 0:30 1:00 2:00" }`; `:ETC` allows others too). (`org-global-properties`)

org_clock_into_drawer.markdownDescription: Where `CLOCK:` lines go: `true` for the drawer of `org_log_into_drawer` (`LOGBOOK` when that is not a name), the name of a drawer, or `false` for the entry itself. (`org-clock-into-drawer`)

org_clock_out_remove_zero_time_clocks.markdownDescription: Clocking out after less than a minute removes the `CLOCK:` line. (`org-clock-out-remove-zero-time-clocks`)

org_clock_out_when_done.markdownDescription: Marking the clocked entry done stops the clock. (`org-clock-out-when-done`)

org_clock_display_default_range.markdownDescription: The span whose clocks `org.clock.display` (`C-c C-x C-d`) adds up. (`org-clock-display-default-range`)

org_clock_idle_time.markdownDescription: After how many minutes without a message from the editor a clock that runs asks what to do with the idle time: keep it, subtract it (and clock out), or cancel the clock. (`org-clock-idle-time`)

org_clock_history_length.markdownDescription: How many entries clocked into the clock history keeps, for `org.clock.in` with a count and `org.clock.in.last`. (`org-clock-history-length`)

org_clock_clocktable_default_properties.markdownDescription: The parameters a new clock table gets on its `#+BEGIN:` line from `org.clock.report` (`C-c C-x C-r`), after `:scope`, as Emacs Lisp reads them (`:maxlevel 3 :link t`). (`org-clock-clocktable-default-properties`)

org_clocktable_defaults.markdownDescription: The parameters every clock table has unless its `#+BEGIN:` line gives them, as Emacs Lisp reads them. Set, it replaces Org's whole list. (`org-clocktable-defaults`)

org_clock_clocktable_language_setup.markdownDescription: The words of a clock table in each language its `:lang` names: the language, then its words for `File`, `L`, `Timestamp`, `Headline`, `Time`, `ALL`, `Total time`, `File time` and `Clock summary at`. A word left out stays English. Set, it replaces Org's languages. (`org-clock-clocktable-language-setup`)

org_clock_report_include_clocking_task.markdownDescription: A clock table counts the time of the clock that runs, for its entry, when the table covers a time (`:block`, `:tstart` and `:tend`) and the clock started within it. (`org-clock-report-include-clocking-task`)

org_clock_rounding_minutes.markdownDescription: Clocking in and out happens at the multiple of this many minutes nearest now; a clock never starts later than now. Below 1, at the minute. (`org-clock-rounding-minutes`)

org_clock_continuously.markdownDescription: A clock starts when the last one stopped, not now. (`org-clock-continuously`)

org_clock_total_time_cell_format.markdownDescription: How a clock table writes its total time and the words before it; `%s` is the text. (`org-clock-total-time-cell-format`)

org_clock_file_time_cell_format.markdownDescription: How a clock table over several files writes the words before a file's time; `%s` is the text. (`org-clock-file-time-cell-format`)

org_clock_in_switch_to_state.markdownDescription: The TODO state an entry is put in when the clock starts on it (`NEXT`), unless it has it already. (`org-clock-in-switch-to-state`)

org_clock_out_switch_to_state.markdownDescription: The TODO state an entry is put in when the clock stops on it. (`org-clock-out-switch-to-state`)

org_lint.markdownDescription: Org's linter checks the documents and reports what it finds as diagnostics: misplaced headings and planning lines, links to nowhere, duplicate names, footnotes without definitions… What it finds is information, a hint for a checker Org trusts little: an Org file is text, nothing in it is an error or a warning. (`org-lint`)

org_lint_ignore.markdownDescription: The `org-lint` checkers to leave out, by name, as a diagnostic's code shows it (`"misplaced-heading"`). (`org-lint`)

org_id_method.markdownDescription: How a new `ID` is made (`org.id.create`, a link stored by ID, org-roam): a random UUID, the time in base 36 (`org`), or the time as `org_id_ts_format` writes it (`ts`). (`org-id-method`)

org_id_prefix.markdownDescription: What a new `ID` starts with, before a colon: `"Org"` makes `Org:…`. (`org-id-prefix`)

org_id_ts_format.markdownDescription: How the `ts` method writes the time, as `format-time-string` does. (`org-id-ts-format`)

org_id_include_domain.markdownDescription: The `org` and `ts` methods end a new `ID` with `@` and the machine's domain. (`org-id-include-domain`)

org_id_track_globally.markdownDescription: IDs are looked for in other files than the link's own: those of `org_id_search_archives`, `org_id_extra_files` and `org_id_locations_file`, the agenda files, the open ones and org-roam's. Off, an `id:` link leads only within its file. (`org-id-track-globally`)

org_id_search_archives.markdownDescription: IDs are looked for in the archive files of the agenda files too. (`org-id-search-archives`)

org_id_extra_files.markdownDescription: More files to look for IDs in: paths or glob patterns. (`org-id-extra-files`)

org_id_locations_file.markdownDescription: The file where Emacs keeps the files it found IDs in: org-lsp looks in them too, and never writes it. Names in it that are not absolute are relative to its directory. (`org-id-locations-file`)

files.description: `current` (the entry's own file), `agenda`, `org-id-files` (the files with IDs), a path or a list of paths

maxlevel.description: The headlines up to this level

todo.description: The headlines with this TODO keyword

regexp.description: The headlines that match this regular expression

org_id_completion_targets.markdownDescription: The headlines an `id:` link completes to (`org.link.insert`), as `org_refile_targets` names them: by default every headline of the file and of the files with IDs. (`org-id-completion-targets`)

org_link_search_must_match_exact_headlin.markdownDescription: What a link to a headline that is not there does: `"query-to-create"` asks whether to make it, at the end of the file, when the link is followed (`org.open`); `true` is an error; `false` looks for its words in the text. (`org-link-search-must-match-exact-headline`)

org_link_doi_server_url.markdownDescription: What a `doi:` link is opened at: this, then the DOI. (`org-link-doi-server-url`)

org_id_link_to_org_use_id.markdownDescription: Whether `org.link.store` (`C-c l`) links to an entry by its ID: `true` makes one when the entry has none, `"create-if-interactive"` only from the command (not for capture's `%a`), `"create-if-interactive-and-no-custom-id"` likewise unless the entry has a `CUSTOM_ID`, `"use-existing"` only when it has one already. Off, the link searches for the headline. (`org-id-link-to-org-use-id`)

org_link_context_for_files.markdownDescription: Links to a place in a file search for it (`file:notes.org::*Heading`); `C-u` turns it around for one link. (`org-link-context-for-files`)

org_id_link_use_context.markdownDescription: ID links to a place below the entry's headline search for it as well (`id:…::name`). (`org-id-link-use-context`)

org_id_link_consider_parent_id.markdownDescription: An ID link may use the ID of a parent entry, with a search for the place. (`org-id-link-consider-parent-id`)

org_link_file_path_type.markdownDescription: How links to files write the path: `"adaptive"` relative below the file's directory and absolute elsewhere, `"absolute"` (with `~`), `"noabbrev"` (without), `"relative"`. (`org-link-file-path-type`)

org_link_keep_stored_after_insertion.markdownDescription: Stored links stay stored once inserted. (`org-link-keep-stored-after-insertion`)

org_complete_tags_always_offer_all_agend.markdownDescription: Completing a tag offers the tags of every agenda file, after those of the file. Off, only the file's own. Setting tags offers them too. (`org-complete-tags-always-offer-all-agenda-tags`)

org_cite_global_bibliography.markdownDescription: Bibliography files for the citations of every document (`[cite:@key]`), after those its `#+BIBLIOGRAPHY:` lines name: BibTeX (`.bib`, `.bibtex`) or CSL-JSON (`.json`). Their entries are completed after `@`, shown over a key, and where following a key goes; a key none has is marked. (`org-cite-global-bibliography`)

org_link_abbrev_alist.markdownDescription: Link abbreviations: `[[gh:org-lsp]]` with `{ "gh": "https://github.com/%s" }` follows `https://github.com/org-lsp`. `%s` stands for what follows the colon, `%h` for it URL-encoded; without either it goes at the end. A file's `#+LINK:` lines come first. `%(my-function)` calls an Emacs function with what follows the colon (through Emacs). (`org-link-abbrev-alist`)

org_tag_alist.markdownDescription: The tags offered when setting tags in a file without a `#+TAGS:` line, written like one: `"work(w) home(h) { @office(o) @home(m) } [ GTD : Control Persp ]"` gives `work` the key `w`, makes `@office` and `@home` exclusive, and groups `Control` and `Persp` under `GTD`; `\n` starts a new line. A list of these words does as well. Unset, the tags used in the file are offered. (`org-tag-alist`)

org_tag_persistent_alist.markdownDescription: Tags offered in every file, before those of `#+TAGS:` or `org_tag_alist`, written the same way. (`org-tag-persistent-alist`)

org_group_tags.markdownDescription: A group tag (`[ GTD : Control Persp ]`, `{ Context : @home @office }` in `#+TAGS:` or `org_tag_alist`) in the match string of a tags view stands for itself and the tags of its group. (`org-group-tags`)

org_use_fast_todo_selection.markdownDescription: How `C-c C-t` (`org.todo`) changes the TODO state where keywords have keys (`TODO(t)`): `auto` picks the state by key from a menu of them; `expert` by key too, the keys listed in the prompt alone (in Neovim and Vim; other editors show their menu); `false` goes to the next state, as where no keyword has a key. `true` is `auto`. (`org-use-fast-todo-selection`)

org_use_fast_tag_selection.markdownDescription: Pick tags by key, each key turning its tag on or off until RET: `auto` when some tag has a key, `true` always (keys are given to the tags without one), `false` never: the tags are typed instead. (`org-use-fast-tag-selection`)

org_fast_tag_selection_single_key.markdownDescription: In fast tag selection, the first key that changes the tags also ends it. (`org-fast-tag-selection-single-key`)

org_tags_sort_function.markdownDescription: Sort the tags of a headline when they are set: alphabetically, or the other way. (`org-tags-sort-function`)

org_auto_align_tags.markdownDescription: Align the tags of a headline to `org_tags_column` when they are set. (`org-auto-align-tags`)

org_todo_repeat_to_state.markdownDescription: The state a repeating entry returns to when it is done: a keyword, or `true` for the state it had. (`org-todo-repeat-to-state`)

org_priority_default.markdownDescription: The priority of an entry without a cookie. A file's `#+PRIORITIES:` line takes precedence over the three priority options. (`org-priority-default`)

org_priority_start_cycle_with_default.markdownDescription: Raising or lowering the priority of an entry that has none starts at the default. (`org-priority-start-cycle-with-default`)

org_time_stamp_rounding_minutes.markdownDescription: The step in which the minutes of a timestamp change (the second number of Org's option). (`org-time-stamp-rounding-minutes`)

org_read_date_prefer_future.markdownDescription: A date typed without a year or month is the next one to come. With `time`, a time that has passed today is tomorrow's. (`org-read-date-prefer-future`)

org_read_date_force_compatible_dates.markdownDescription: A typed year is kept within 1970 to 2037. (`org-read-date-force-compatible-dates`)

files.description: `current` (the entry's own file), `agenda`, `org-id-files` (the files with IDs), a path or a list of paths

maxlevel.description: The headlines up to this level

todo.description: The headlines with this TODO keyword

regexp.description: The headlines that match this regular expression

org_refile_targets.markdownDescription: Where entries can be refiled to. Each entry has `files`: `current` (the entry's own file), `agenda`, `org-id-files` (the files with IDs), a path or a list of paths; and one of `level`, `maxlevel`, `tag`, `todo`, `regexp` (the Rust `regex` crate's syntax) or `all` (true), which says which headlines there are targets. (`org-refile-targets`)

org_refile_use_outline_path.markdownDescription: Name targets by their outline path (`Projects/Alpha/`). The three names start the path with the file, and offer the file itself, for its top level. (`org-refile-use-outline-path`)

org_refile_allow_creating_parent_nodes.markdownDescription: A target that is not there yet can be named after an existing one, `Projects/New`: it is made, as the last child of `Projects`, and the entry goes under it. `confirm` asks first. (`org-refile-allow-creating-parent-nodes`)

org_refile_target_verify_function.markdownDescription: The name of an Emacs Lisp function that decides which headlines are refile targets: the server's Emacs calls it at the start of each, and keeps those it says yes to. Where it leaves the point, the search goes on: a function can skip a subtree. (`org-refile-target-verify-function`)

org_reverse_note_order.markdownDescription: A refiled entry goes first under its target, not last. (`org-reverse-note-order`)

org_archive_location.markdownDescription: Where archived subtrees go: a file, `::`, and a headline under which they go (they go to the end of the file without one). `%s` is the name of the file the subtree is in; an empty file part is that file. `datetree/` as the headline files them under year, month and day, by when they were closed. An `ARCHIVE` property of the entry or a parent, or a `#+ARCHIVE:` line, says otherwise. (`org-archive-location`)

org_archive_reversed_order.markdownDescription: An archived subtree goes first under its archive headline, not last. (`org-archive-reversed-order`)

org_archive_mark_done.markdownDescription: Mark archived entries done: `true` for the first done keyword, or the keyword to use. (`org-archive-mark-done`)

org_archive_subtree_add_inherited_tags.markdownDescription: Give an archived subtree the tags it inherited: always, never, or when it stays in its file. (`org-archive-subtree-add-inherited-tags`)

org_archive_save_context_info.markdownDescription: What an archived entry keeps as `ARCHIVE_…` properties: `time`, `file`, `olpath` (its outline path), `category`, `todo`, `itags` (inherited tags), `ltags` (its own tags) and `olid` (its parent's ID). (`org-archive-save-context-info`)

org_archive_sibling_heading.markdownDescription: The headline of the sibling `org.archive.sibling` archives under. (`org-archive-sibling-heading`)

org_archive_file_header_format.markdownDescription: What a new archive file starts with; `%s` is the path of the file the subtree came from. (`org-archive-file-header-format`)

org_archive_default_command.markdownDescription: What `org.archive.default` does: archive the subtree, archive it under its sibling, or tag it. (`org-archive-default-command`)

key.description: The keys the context is about

use.description: The keys whose template or command these keys stand for where the context holds

contexts.description: Rules, each a regexp on the file, the mode or the buffer's name; the context holds where one of them does

org_capture_templates_contexts.markdownDescription: Where templates are offered. Each has the `key` of a template, `contexts`, rules such as `{ "in_file": "work" }` (`in_file`, `in_mode`, `in_buffer`, `not_in_file`, `not_in_mode` or `not_in_buffer`, each with a regexp of the `regex` crate's syntax, matched ignoring case), and maybe `use`, the key of the template it stands for there. A template with contexts is offered only where one of their rules holds. The mode is `org-mode` in an Org file and `org-agenda-mode` in the agenda, where there is no file; the buffer's name is the file's. (`org-capture-templates-contexts`)

key.description: The keys that pick the template

type.description: An Org entry (the default), plain text, a list item, a checkbox item or a table line

target.description: `file` and a path; `file+headline`, a path and a headline; `file+olp`, a path and the headlines of an outline path; `file+regexp`, a path and a regular expression; `file+olp+datetree`, a path and maybe an outline path; `id` and an ID; `clock`; `file+function`, a path and an Emacs Lisp function; or `function` and an Emacs Lisp function that visits the file

prepend.description: First under the target, not last

tree_type.description: The levels of a date tree

time_prompt.description: Ask for the date of the date tree entry

table_line_pos.description: Where a table line goes: `II-1` is above the second rule

clock_in.description: Clock the captured entry while the capture goes on

clock_keep.description: Keep the clock running when the capture is filed

clock_resume.description: Start the clock the capture stopped again

jump_to_captured.description: Show the captured entry in its file

unnarrowed.description: Show the whole target file in the capture buffer

org_capture_templates.markdownDescription: Capture templates. Each has a `key`, a `description`, a `type` (`entry`, the default, `plain`, `item`, `checkitem` or `table-line`), a `target` and a `template` (text, or a list of lines), and may have `prepend`, `empty_lines`, `empty_lines_before`, `empty_lines_after`, `immediate_finish`, `tree_type`, `time_prompt`, `table_line_pos`, `clock_in`, `clock_keep`, `clock_resume`, `jump_to_captured` and `unnarrowed`. The target is a list: `file` and a path; `file+headline`, a path and a headline; `file+olp`, a path and the headlines of an outline path; `file+regexp`, a path and a regular expression; `file+olp+datetree`, a path and the headlines of an outline path, maybe none, for a date tree under them; `id` and an ID; `clock`, the entry clocked now; `file+function`, a path and the name of an Emacs Lisp function that moves the point there, or `function` and the name of one that visits the file too (run by the server's Emacs). An empty path is `org_default_notes_file`, and without a target the entry goes at the end of `org_default_notes_file`. A template with only a key and a description groups the templates whose keys start with its key. (`org-capture-templates`)

org_directory.markdownDescription: Where the relative paths of capture targets are. (`org-directory`)

org_default_notes_file.markdownDescription: The target of a capture template whose file is empty. (`org-default-notes-file`)

org_link_descriptive.markdownDescription: Show a link as its description (or its target, when it has none) and hide the rest: the brackets, and the target of a link with a description. The text is marked `hidden` in the highlighting, and editors that can conceal text conceal it. (`org-link-descriptive`)

org_hide_emphasis_markers.markdownDescription: Hide the markers around `*bold*`, `/italic/`, `_underline_`, `+strike-through+`, `=verbatim=` and `~code~`, as for links. (`org-hide-emphasis-markers`)

org_fontify_emphasized_text.markdownDescription: Show `*bold*`, `/italic/`, `_underline_`, `+strike-through+`, `=verbatim=` and `~code~` in their looks. With `false` they look as the text around them, their markers shown. (`org-fontify-emphasized-text`)

org_emphasis_alist.markdownDescription: The look of each kind of emphasis, by its marker (`*`, `/`, `_`, `=`, `~`, `+`): a face of Org's, `bold`, `italic`, `bold-italic`, `underline`, `org-code` or `org-verbatim`, attributes as Org writes them (`:weight bold :slant italic :underline t :strike-through t`), or a list of them; `false` for none. As in Emacs, a marker left out has no look. Colors are not shown. (`org-emphasis-alist`)

org_hidden_keywords.markdownDescription: The keywords hidden before their values, such as `#+TITLE:` with `["title"]`, in editors that conceal text. (`org-hidden-keywords`)

org_hide_macro_markers.markdownDescription: Hide the braces of macro calls, `{{{` and `}}}`, in editors that conceal text. (`org-hide-macro-markers`)

org_pretty_entities.markdownDescription: Show entities (`\alpha`, `\to`) as their character (`α`, `→`): the entity is hidden as link brackets are, and its character is an inlay hint in its place. (`org-pretty-entities`)

org_pretty_entities_include_sub_superscr.markdownDescription: With `org_pretty_entities`, show sub- and superscripts (`x^2`, `H_{2}O`, `a_{n}`) raised and lowered: in Unicode (`x²`, `H₂O`, `aₙ`) where every character has a raised or lowered form, as an inlay hint in place of the hidden text; the others are left as they are. (`org-pretty-entities-include-sub-superscripts`)

org_use_sub_superscripts.markdownDescription: Which sub- and superscripts `org_pretty_entities` shows: all, only those in braces (`a_{b}`, `"{}"`), or none. (`org-use-sub-superscripts`)

return_uses_meta_return.markdownDescription: RET on the first line of a list item makes the next item, numbered and with a checkbox as M-RET (`org-meta-return`) makes it, the items after it renumbered, as nvim-orgmode's `org_return_uses_meta_return` does. Off, RET is Org's: a new line in the item. `org.return.item` (`<S-CR>`, Shift+Enter, with the vim keys) always does it.

org_return_follows_link.markdownDescription: RET (`org.return`) on a link, a timestamp or a citation follows it, as `org.open` (`C-c C-o`) does. In a table RET still moves down. (`org-return-follows-link`)

calendar_months.markdownDescription: How many months the calendar of the date prompt shows: 3 side by side, as Emacs's calendar shows them, the one with the selected day in the middle; or 1, that month alone, for a narrow window, with the answer on a line under the prompt.

calendar_week_start_day.markdownDescription: The day the weeks of the date prompt's calendar start on: 1 starts them on Monday. (`calendar-week-start-day`)

emacs.markdownDescription: The Emacs program, for what only Org itself does: export (`org.export.dispatch`). The server starts it (`emacs --batch -Q`) when that is first asked for and keeps it running, so that Org loads once. Without Emacs, everything else works as before.

emacs_config_file.markdownDescription: A file of Emacs Lisp that Emacs loads before Org, for the variables export reads (`org-export-backends`, `org-html-…`, `org-latex-…`, `org-publish-project-alist`): a file of its own, or your init file. `~/` is the home directory.

emacs_config.markdownDescription: Emacs Lisp that Emacs evaluates after `emacs_config_file` and before loading Org, for a few settings without a file: `(setq org-export-with-toc nil)`, or `(add-to-list 'load-path "~/src/org-mode/lisp")` for another Org. A yes-or-no question Emacs asks while it works (`org-confirm-babel-evaluate`) is asked in the editor.

auto_save.markdownDescription: Save the files a command changes other than the one it was run in: an entry's file changed from the agenda, the target of a capture or of a refile. The editor saves them once it has made the change. Off, they are left with unsaved changes, as Emacs leaves them.

org_cycle_separator_lines.markdownDescription: With at least this many blank lines after a subtree, the last one stays outside its fold. Negative: all of them stay outside. `0`: none does. (`org-cycle-separator-lines`)

org_cycle_include_plain_lists.markdownDescription: Whether list items fold, as subtrees do. `integrate` makes them part of the outline: TAB showing a headline's children folds its lists to their top items too. `false`: they do not fold. (`org-cycle-include-plain-lists`)

org_cycle_max_level.markdownDescription: The deepest headlines that fold; deeper ones are text of the subtree they are in. (`org-cycle-max-level`)

org_cycle_global_at_bob.markdownDescription: TAB at the very start of the file, when its first line is no headline, cycles the whole file as S-TAB does. (`org-cycle-global-at-bob`)

org_cycle_level_after_item_entry_creatio.markdownDescription: TAB on a new, empty headline makes it a child of the headline before, then each level up, then a sibling again; on an empty item, it indents and outdents the item the same way. (`org-cycle-level-after-item/entry-creation`)

org_startup_folded.markdownDescription: How files show when opened: `"overview"` (or `"fold"`) only the top headlines, `"content"` all the headlines, `"show2levels"` to `"show5levels"` the headlines down to that level, `"showeverything"` (or `"nofold"`, `"showall"`) everything. `#+STARTUP:` decides for a file. Unless everything shows, a subtree's `VISIBILITY` property (`folded`, `children`, `content`, `all`) decides for it, archived subtrees are folded, and drawers too. Folds hide whole subtrees, so where Org shows a headline's children but not its text, the text shows. (`org-startup-folded`)

org_startup_shrink_all_tables.markdownDescription: Shrink the columns of every table that have a width cookie (`<10>`) when a file opens. `#+STARTUP: shrink` decides for a file. Shrunk fields show their first characters and `…`, in editors that can hide text. (`org-startup-shrink-all-tables`)

org_cycle_hide_block_startup.markdownDescription: Fold blocks when a file opens folded (`org_startup_folded`). `#+STARTUP: hideblocks` and `nohideblocks` decide for a file. (`org-cycle-hide-block-startup`)

org_cycle_hide_drawer_startup.markdownDescription: Fold drawers when a file opens folded (`org_startup_folded`). (`org-cycle-hide-drawer-startup`)

org_cycle_open_archived_trees.markdownDescription: Leave archived subtrees open when a file opens folded (`org_startup_folded`). (`org-cycle-open-archived-trees`)

org_adapt_indentation.markdownDescription: Indent the lines of an entry past its headline's stars: `true` for all of them, `"headline-data"` for the planning line, drawers and clock lines right below the headline. Applies to new lines, to re-indenting (range formatting) and to what commands write. (`org-adapt-indentation`)

org_image_actual_width.markdownDescription: How wide the image of a link shows: `true` at its own width; a number, that many pixels; `false` or a list of one number, the `:width` of the paragraph's `#+ATTR_ORG:` or else of another `#+ATTR_…:` (pixels, `50%` or a fraction up to 2 of the text's width, `t` for its own width), else the list's number. An entry's `ORG-IMAGE-ACTUAL-WIDTH` property decides for its own text. (`org-image-actual-width`)

org_image_max_width.markdownDescription: How wide at most an image shown at its own width is: `"fill-column"`, 70 columns; `"window"`, the window's width; an integer, that many pixels; a float, that part of the window's width; null for no limit. (`org-image-max-width`)

org_startup_with_link_previews.markdownDescription: Show the images of links to image files in place when a file opens, as `C-c C-x C-v` (`org.link.preview`) shows them. `#+STARTUP: inlineimages` (or `linkpreviews`) and `noinlineimages` decide for a file. Editors that can show images: Neovim from 0.13 (`vim.ui.img`), in a terminal with the Kitty graphics protocol. (`org-startup-with-link-previews`)

org_startup_with_latex_preview.markdownDescription: Show the LaTeX fragments as images when a file opens, as `C-c C-x C-l` (`org.latex.preview`) shows them, made by Emacs. `#+STARTUP: latexpreview` and `nolatexpreview` decide for a file. (`org-startup-with-latex-preview`)

org_startup_indented.markdownDescription: Show files indented by level without changing them (`org-indent-mode`): the text under a headline lines up with its title, and leading stars are hidden. `#+STARTUP: indent` and `noindent` decide for a file. It turns `org_adapt_indentation` off in such files, unless that is `"headline-data"`. Editors that can show it: Neovim, and VS Code (not on wrapped lines). (`org-startup-indented`)

org_hide_leading_stars.markdownDescription: Hide all the stars of a headline but the last; they keep their place. `#+STARTUP: hidestars` and `showstars` decide for a file. (`org-hide-leading-stars`)

org_duration_format.markdownDescription: How durations are written (clock tables, clock lines, efforts): `"h:mm"` or `"h:mm:ss"`, or a list of units each with whether it is written when zero (`["d", false]`), with perhaps `["special", "h:mm"]` (the hours and minutes as `H:MM` after the larger units), `["special", "h:mm:ss"]`, `["special", 2]` (one unit with 2 decimals) and `"compact"` (no space between units). The units are those of `org_duration_units`. (`org-duration-format`)

org_duration_units.markdownDescription: The units of durations and the minutes in each, for reading efforts and writing durations: `["d", 480]` for days of 8 hours. (`org-duration-units`)

org_fontify_done_headline.markdownDescription: Show a headline marked done in the look of done headlines past its keyword (`org-headline-done`). (`org-fontify-done-headline`)

org_fontify_todo_headline.markdownDescription: Show a headline marked with a keyword not done in the look of TODO headlines past its keyword (`org-headline-todo`, the token modifier `todo`). (`org-fontify-todo-headline`)

org_fontify_quote_and_verse_blocks.markdownDescription: Show the lines inside quote and verse blocks in their own look (`org-quote`, `org-verse`: the token types `quote` and `verse`). (`org-fontify-quote-and-verse-blocks`)

org_ellipsis.markdownDescription: What a closed fold shows after its first line, such as `" ▾"`, in the highlight group `OrgLspEllipsis` (Neovim). Editors that can show it: Neovim and Vim. (`org-ellipsis`)

org_bullets_mode.markdownDescription: org-bullets: the last star of each headline shows as a bullet, those of `org_bullets_bullet_list` by level, and the stars before it are hidden, as with `org_hide_leading_stars`. (`org-bullets-mode`)

org_bullets_bullet_list.markdownDescription: The bullets of `org_bullets_mode`, one a level, repeating after the last. (`org-bullets-bullet-list`)

org_bullets_list_bullet.markdownDescription: What `org_bullets_mode` shows in place of the `-`, `+` or `*` of an item, as org-bullets.nvim does; `false` leaves them as they are.

org_bullets_checkboxes.markdownDescription: What `org_bullets_mode` shows between the brackets of a checkbox, `[ ]`, `[-]` and `[X]`, as org-bullets.nvim does; `false` leaves them as they are. A state left out keeps its default.

org_src_preserve_indentation.markdownDescription: Leave the code of source blocks as it is indented when re-indenting. (`org-src-preserve-indentation`)

org_src_content_indentation.markdownDescription: How far code is indented past its source block: when re-indenting, and when the code of a block edited in a file of its own (`C-c '`) is written back. Formerly `org_edit_src_content_indentation`, which is still read. (`org-src-content-indentation`)

org_agenda_span.markdownDescription: How much time the agenda shows. (`org-agenda-span`)

org_agenda_start_on_weekday.markdownDescription: The day a week or fortnight starts on; `false` starts it today. (`org-agenda-start-on-weekday`)

org_deadline_warning_days.markdownDescription: How many days before a deadline it shows up. (`org-deadline-warning-days`)

org_scheduled_delay_days.markdownDescription: How many days after its date a scheduled entry shows up. (`org-scheduled-delay-days`)

org_scheduled_past_days.markdownDescription: How many days a scheduled entry that is not done keeps showing up. (`org-scheduled-past-days`)

org_modules.markdownDescription: Org modules to load. `org-habit` turns habits on: entries with the `STYLE` property `habit` and a scheduled date with a repeater (`.+2d`, `.+2d/4d` for a deadline too) show in the agenda with a graph of the days they were done. Others are ignored. (`org-modules`)

org_habit_graph_column.markdownDescription: The column the consistency graph of a habit starts at in the agenda. (`org-habit-graph-column`)

org_habit_preceding_days.markdownDescription: How many days before today a habit's graph shows. (`org-habit-preceding-days`)

org_habit_following_days.markdownDescription: How many days after today a habit's graph shows. (`org-habit-following-days`)

org_habit_show_habits_only_for_today.markdownDescription: Show habits only on today's date, not on future days of the agenda. (`org-habit-show-habits-only-for-today`)

org_habit_show_all_today.markdownDescription: Show every habit today, even those not scheduled for today. (`org-habit-show-all-today`)

org_habit_today_glyph.markdownDescription: The mark of today in a habit's graph. (`org-habit-today-glyph`)

org_habit_completed_glyph.markdownDescription: The mark of a day a habit was done in its graph. (`org-habit-completed-glyph`)

org_habit_show_done_always_green.markdownDescription: A day a habit was done is green in its graph even when it was done late. (`org-habit-show-done-always-green`)

org_habit_scheduled_past_days.markdownDescription: How many days a habit that is not done keeps showing up. (`org-habit-scheduled-past-days`)

org_deadline_past_days.markdownDescription: How many days a missed deadline keeps showing up. (`org-deadline-past-days`)

org_agenda_skip_scheduled_if_done.markdownDescription: Leave out scheduled entries that are done. (`org-agenda-skip-scheduled-if-done`)

org_agenda_skip_deadline_if_done.markdownDescription: Leave out deadlines of entries that are done. (`org-agenda-skip-deadline-if-done`)

org_agenda_skip_timestamp_if_done.markdownDescription: Leave out timestamps of entries that are done. (`org-agenda-skip-timestamp-if-done`)

org_agenda_time_leading_zero.markdownDescription: Write times with two digits for the hour (`08:00`). (`org-agenda-time-leading-zero`)

org_agenda_timegrid_use_ampm.markdownDescription: Write the times of the agenda, the time grid's too, in 12-hour form (`8:00am`). (`org-agenda-timegrid-use-ampm`)

org_agenda_search_headline_for_time.markdownDescription: Take a time in a headline (`Call at 15:00`) as the time of its entry. (`org-agenda-search-headline-for-time`)

org_agenda_remove_times_when_in_prefix.markdownDescription: Take a time out of the headline when the prefix shows it; `beg` only one at the start of the headline. (`org-agenda-remove-times-when-in-prefix`)

org_agenda_default_appointment_duration.markdownDescription: Minutes an entry with a start time and no end time lasts: the agenda shows it as a range. (`org-agenda-default-appointment-duration`)

org_agenda_remove_timeranges_from_blocks.markdownDescription: Take a date range out of the headline of its lines. (`org-agenda-remove-timeranges-from-blocks`)

org_agenda_diary_sexp_prefix.markdownDescription: A regexp (Emacs's syntax): what it matches of a diary sexp's text goes in front of the line, as a scheduled date's `Scheduled:` does. (`org-agenda-diary-sexp-prefix`)

org_agenda_show_inherited_tags.markdownDescription: Show the inherited tags of an entry on its agenda lines: where `org_agenda_use_tag_inheritance` has them (`true`), always, never (`false`), or in these kinds of views (`agenda`, `todo`, `search`). Sorting by tag and `org_agenda_max_tags` go by the tags a line shows. (`org-agenda-show-inherited-tags`)

org_agenda_use_tag_inheritance.markdownDescription: The kinds of views whose lines have inherited tags (`true`: all). Tags matches always have them. (`org-agenda-use-tag-inheritance`)

org_agenda_hide_tags_regexp.markdownDescription: A regexp (Emacs's syntax): the tags it matches are not shown on agenda lines, but filters still see them. (`org-agenda-hide-tags-regexp`)

org_agenda_skip_additional_timestamps_sa.markdownDescription: Once a timestamp of an entry has made a line for a day, leave out its other timestamps on that day. (`org-agenda-skip-additional-timestamps-same-entry`)

org_agenda_fontify_priorities.markdownDescription: Highlight the priority cookies of agenda lines (`cookies`), or each line from its cookie on (`true`; links and tags keep their own look); the highest priority shows in bold, the lowest in italic. `false` highlights none. Org's list of faces by priority is not read here: `org_priority_faces` gives them. (`org-agenda-fontify-priorities`)

org_agenda_prefer_last_repeat.markdownDescription: Show a repeating scheduled date, deadline or timestamp at its last repeat up to today instead of its base date, for every entry (`true`) or for those with one of these TODO keywords. (`org-agenda-prefer-last-repeat`)

org_agenda_skip_deadline_prewarning_if_s.markdownDescription: For a scheduled entry, show its deadline only on its date (`true`), not before its scheduled date (`pre-scheduled`), or from N days before it (a number). (`org-agenda-skip-deadline-prewarning-if-scheduled`)

org_agenda_skip_scheduled_delay_if_deadl.markdownDescription: For an entry with a deadline, drop the delay of its scheduled date (`--2d`) (`true`), or keep it no later than the deadline (`post-deadline`). A number drops it too, as Org's code does. (`org-agenda-skip-scheduled-delay-if-deadline`)

org_agenda_skip_scheduled_if_deadline_is.markdownDescription: Leave out a scheduled date on a day its entry's deadline shows (`true`), only when it was scheduled before today (`not-today`); `repeated-after-deadline` is `org_agenda_skip_scheduled_repeats_after_deadline`. Not for habits. (`org-agenda-skip-scheduled-if-deadline-is-shown`)

org_agenda_skip_scheduled_repeats_after_.markdownDescription: Leave out the repeats of a scheduled date that come after the entry's deadline. (`org-agenda-skip-scheduled-repeats-after-deadline`)

org_agenda_skip_comment_trees.markdownDescription: Leave out of every view the entries of a commented subtree (`COMMENT` after the stars). (`org-agenda-skip-comment-trees`)

org_agenda_todo_list_sublevels.markdownDescription: Show in the TODO list the TODO entries below another one. Off, the list skips the subtree of each entry it shows or leaves out for a date. (`org-agenda-todo-list-sublevels`)

org_agenda_todo_ignore_with_date.markdownDescription: Leave out of the TODO list the entries with an active timestamp anywhere in their text, scheduled and deadline dates too. (`org-agenda-todo-ignore-with-date`)

org_agenda_todo_ignore_scheduled.markdownDescription: Leave out of the TODO list the scheduled entries: all of them (`true`, `all`), those scheduled after today (`future`), today or before (`past`), or with a number N, N days from now or later (a negative N: N days ago or before). (`org-agenda-todo-ignore-scheduled`)

org_agenda_todo_ignore_deadlines.markdownDescription: Leave out of the TODO list the entries with a deadline: in its warning period, that is, shown in the agenda (`true`, `near`), not yet in it (`far`), all of them (`all`), after today (`future`), today or before (`past`), or with a number as for `org_agenda_todo_ignore_scheduled`. (`org-agenda-todo-ignore-deadlines`)

org_agenda_todo_ignore_timestamp.markdownDescription: Leave out of the TODO list the entries with an active timestamp that is no scheduled or deadline date, with the values of `org_agenda_todo_ignore_scheduled`. (`org-agenda-todo-ignore-timestamp`)

org_agenda_todo_ignore_time_comparison_u.markdownDescription: Compare the dates of the `org_agenda_todo_ignore_*` settings with now to the second instead of by day: `future` is then later than now, and a number counts seconds. (`org-agenda-todo-ignore-time-comparison-use-seconds`)

org_agenda_tags_todo_honor_ignore_option.markdownDescription: Have the `org_agenda_todo_ignore_*` settings leave entries out of `tags-todo` matches as well. (`org-agenda-tags-todo-honor-ignore-options`)

org_agenda_sorting_strategy.markdownDescription: How the lines of a day (`agenda`), the TODO list (`todo`), a tags match (`tags`, `tags-todo` too) and a search (`search`) are ordered: the strategies in turn, each deciding when the ones before do not. A view without a list takes `agenda`'s, and without that `time-up`, `category-keep`, `urgency-down`; one list alone is for every view. `time-up`/`-down` the time of day; `timestamp-`, `scheduled-`, `deadline-`, `ts-` (active) and `tsia-` (inactive) `up`/`down` the date of that kind (in the TODO list and a tags match, the entry's); `priority-` the priority, `urgency-` the priority with how near or overdue the date is; `effort-`, `category-` (and `category-keep`, the order the entries come in), `tag-` (the last tag), `todo-state-` (where the keyword is in the file's list, done ones first), `habit-`, `alpha-` (the headline), `stats-` (the statistics cookie). `user-defined-up` and `-down` call Lisp, which the server does not run. (`org-agenda-sorting-strategy`)

org_agenda_sort_notime_is_late.markdownDescription: Lines without a time (or without the date a strategy sorts by) come after those with one. (`org-agenda-sort-notime-is-late`)

org_agenda_sort_noeffort_is_high.markdownDescription: Entries without an effort count as having the highest when sorted, filtered or limited by effort. (`org-agenda-sort-noeffort-is-high`)

org_agenda_max_entries.markdownDescription: How many entries a day of the agenda, the TODO list, a tags match or a search shows at most: one number for all, or one for each kind of view. Other lines, such as those of the time grid, go as well; with a negative number they stay. (`org-agenda-max-entries`)

org_agenda_max_todos.markdownDescription: How many entries with a TODO keyword a view shows at most, the other lines going as well; with a negative number, those stay. (`org-agenda-max-todos`)

org_agenda_max_tags.markdownDescription: How many entries with tags a view shows at most, the other lines going as well; with a negative number, those stay. (`org-agenda-max-tags`)

org_agenda_max_effort.markdownDescription: The most minutes of effort the entries of a view add up to: entries show while their efforts, in order, stay within it (an entry without one counts as the highest, or as -1 with `org_agenda_sort_noeffort_is_high` off). (`org-agenda-max-effort`)

org_agenda_show_future_repeats.markdownDescription: Show the future dates of repeating entries: all of them, none, or only the next. (`org-agenda-show-future-repeats`)

org_agenda_tags_column.markdownDescription: Where tags are aligned in the agenda: a column (negative: where they end), or `auto` for the right edge of the window. With `auto`, the editors that tell the server how wide the agenda's window is (Neovim, Vim, Sublime Text) have the tags there, and the agenda follows the window as it is resized; the others (VS Code, Zed) have them end at column 80. (`org-agenda-tags-column`)

org_agenda_time_grid.markdownDescription: The time grid, as Org writes it: the days that have it (`daily`: a one-day agenda; `weekly`: every day of a longer one; `today`: today; `require-timed`: only days with an entry that has a time; `remove-match`: no grid line at a time an entry already has), the times of its lines (`800` for 8:00), what follows a time that has no end time, and the text of a grid line. (`org-agenda-time-grid`)

org_agenda_current_time_string.markdownDescription: The text of the line for the current time. (`org-agenda-current-time-string`)

org_agenda_show_current_time_in_grid.markdownDescription: Show the current time in the grid. (`org-agenda-show-current-time-in-grid`)

org_agenda_weekend_days.markdownDescription: The days drawn as the weekend (0 is Sunday). (`org-agenda-weekend-days`)

org_agenda_start_with_log_mode.markdownDescription: Start the agenda in log mode, which shows what was closed and clocked each day (`l` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-log-mode`)

org_agenda_start_with_clockreport_mode.markdownDescription: Start the agenda with the clock report under it (`R` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-clockreport-mode`)

org_agenda_clockreport_parameter_plist.markdownDescription: The parameters of the clock report's table, as those of a clock table block (`:maxlevel 3 :tags t`); `:block`, `:tstart`, `:tend` and `:scope` are the agenda's. (`org-agenda-clockreport-parameter-plist`)

org_agenda_clock_report_header.markdownDescription: Text on a line of its own (or lines) before the clock report. (`org-agenda-clock-report-header`)

org_agenda_start_with_archives_mode.markdownDescription: Start the agenda with entries in archived trees (`trees`; `v a` toggles it), or those and the files the agenda files archive to (`files`; `v A`). (`org-agenda-start-with-archives-mode`)

org_agenda_log_mode_items.markdownDescription: What log mode shows: `closed` entries, `clock` lines and `state` changes. (`org-agenda-log-mode-items`)

org_agenda_log_mode_add_notes.markdownDescription: Show the note of a state change or a clock line after the headline in log mode. (`org-agenda-log-mode-add-notes`)

org_agenda_move_date_from_past_immediate.markdownDescription: Moving a date of the past one day later from the agenda (`S-<right>`) takes it to today. (`org-agenda-move-date-from-past-immediately-to-today`)

org_agenda_persistent_marks.markdownDescription: Keep the marks of a bulk action (`B`) after it (`p` in its menu toggles this for one action). (`org-agenda-persistent-marks`)

org_agenda_start_with_follow_mode.markdownDescription: Start the agenda in follow mode, which shows the entry of the cursor's line in another window as the cursor moves (`F` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-follow-mode`)

org_agenda_start_with_entry_text_mode.markdownDescription: Start the agenda with some text of each entry under its line (`E` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-entry-text-mode`)

org_agenda_entry_text_maxlines.markdownDescription: The most lines of an entry's text `E` shows. (`org-agenda-entry-text-maxlines`)

org_agenda_entry_text_leaders.markdownDescription: What each line of an entry's text starts with in the agenda. (`org-agenda-entry-text-leaders`)

org_agenda_entry_text_exclude_regexps.markdownDescription: Emacs regexps whose matches are left out of the entry text `E` shows. (`org-agenda-entry-text-exclude-regexps`)

org_agenda_block_separator.markdownDescription: What goes between the blocks of a block agenda: one character repeated across 79 columns, a longer text as it is, or `false` for nothing. In a block's `settings`, the separator above that block. (`org-agenda-block-separator`)

org_agenda_compact_blocks.markdownDescription: Leave out the separators between blocks and the header over agenda blocks. (`org-agenda-compact-blocks`)

agenda_hide_empty_blocks.markdownDescription: Leave out the blocks of a block agenda that show no entries. Not in Org.

org_super_agenda_mode.markdownDescription: org-super-agenda: show the lines of the agenda's views in the groups of `org_super_agenda_groups`, each under a header. Off, the groups are not used. (`org-super-agenda-mode`)

org_super_agenda_groups.markdownDescription: org-super-agenda's groups, in turn taking the lines they select: each an object of selectors and their arguments in Emacs's order, `{ name = "Today", time-grid = true }`, or a list of them in turn; `true` is `t`, `false` is `nil` (and for `name`, `none`: no header). The lines no group takes come last, under `org_super_agenda_unmatched_name`. In a custom command's `settings`, the groups of that command or block. (`org-super-agenda-groups`)

org_super_agenda_unmatched_name.markdownDescription: The header of the lines no group takes. (`org-super-agenda-unmatched-name`)

org_super_agenda_unmatched_order.markdownDescription: Where the lines no group takes come among the groups: groups show lowest `order` first. (`org-super-agenda-unmatched-order`)

org_super_agenda_header_separator.markdownDescription: What goes before each header: text, or one character repeated across the window, then a newline. (`org-super-agenda-header-separator`)

org_super_agenda_final_group_separator.markdownDescription: What goes after the last group: text put at the end of its last line, or one character repeated across the window on a line of its own. (`org-super-agenda-final-group-separator`)

org_super_agenda_date_format.markdownDescription: The headers of the groups of `auto-planning` and `auto-ts`, as `format-time-string` writes dates. (`org-super-agenda-date-format`)

org_super_agenda_hide_empty_groups.markdownDescription: Leave out the headers of groups whose lines the agenda's filters all hide. (`org-super-agenda-hide-empty-groups`)

org_super_agenda_keep_order.markdownDescription: Sort the lines of each group again, as the view sorts its lines: a group of several selectors puts the lines of its first selector first. (`org-super-agenda-keep-order`)

org_super_agenda_properties_inherit.markdownDescription: Look for the properties of `property`, `auto-property` and `auto-group` in the entries above too. (`org-super-agenda-properties-inherit`)

org_roam_enabled.markdownDescription: org-roam: the files of `org_roam_directory` are a network of notes, whose nodes (files and entries with an `ID`) are found, linked to and made with the `org.roam.*` commands. Off, those commands only say so.

org_roam_directory.markdownDescription: The directory of org-roam's files, in all its subdirectories. `~/` is the home directory. (`org-roam-directory`)

org_roam_file_extensions.markdownDescription: The extensions of org-roam's files; each may be followed by `.gpg` or `.age`, which the server cannot read. (`org-roam-file-extensions`)

org_roam_file_exclude_regexp.markdownDescription: Emacs regexps for the files that are not org-roam's, matched against their names relative to `org_roam_directory`; the default leaves out attachments. (`org-roam-file-exclude-regexp`)

org_roam_node_display_template.markdownDescription: How a node is offered: `${field}` for its `title`, `tags`, `todo`, `file`, `olp`, `aliases` and the other fields of `org-roam-node`, `${field:N}` in N columns, `${field:*}` in what is left of the window's 79 columns. (`org-roam-node-display-template`)

org_roam_link_auto_replace.markdownDescription: Turn the `roam:` links of org-roam's files into `id:` links to their nodes as the files are saved, and as a link is followed. (`org-roam-link-auto-replace`)

org_roam_completion_everywhere.markdownDescription: In org-roam's files, offer the titles of the nodes for the word at the cursor, not only in a link; the one picked becomes a link to its node. (`org-roam-completion-everywhere`)

org_roam_mode_sections.markdownDescription: The sections of the org-roam buffer, in turn: `backlinks` (the nodes that link to the node), `reflinks` (those that link to or cite its references) and `unlinked-references` (the places that name it without a link, found by the server itself). (`org-roam-mode-sections`)

key.description: The keys that pick the template

type.description: An Org entry (the default), plain text, a list item, a checkbox item or a table line

target.description: `file` and a path; `file+head`, a path and the head of a new file; `file+olp`, a path and an outline path; `file+head+olp`, a path, a head and an outline path; or `node` and a node's title, alias or ID

prepend.description: First under the target, not last

unnarrowed.description: Show the whole file in the capture buffer

org_roam_capture_templates.markdownDescription: The templates of new nodes, as `org_capture_templates` writes them, with org-roam's targets: `file` and a path, `file+head`, a path and the text a new file starts with, `file+olp`, a path and the headlines of an outline path, `file+head+olp`, both, and `node` and the title, alias or `ID` of a node. The path, relative to `org_roam_directory`, and the texts may have `${title}`, `${slug}`, `${id}` and `${name}`, which asks for `name` (`${name=default}` starts the answer with `default`), besides the escapes of `org_capture_templates`. `unnarrowed` shows the whole file in the capture buffer. (`org-roam-capture-templates`)

org_roam_dailies_directory.markdownDescription: Where the daily notes are, relative to `org_roam_directory`. (`org-roam-dailies-directory`)

key.description: The keys that pick the template

type.description: An Org entry (the default), plain text, a list item, a checkbox item or a table line

target.description: `file` and a path; `file+head`, a path and the head of a new file; `file+olp`, a path and an outline path; `file+head+olp`, a path, a head and an outline path; or `node` and a node's title, alias or ID

prepend.description: First under the target, not last

unnarrowed.description: Show the whole file in the capture buffer

org_roam_dailies_capture_templates.markdownDescription: The templates of the daily notes, as `org_roam_capture_templates` writes them, with paths relative to `org_roam_dailies_directory`; `%<…>` is the note's day. (`org-roam-dailies-capture-templates`)

org_journal_enabled.markdownDescription: org-journal: a journal in `org_journal_dir`, a file a day (or week, month, year), written with the `org.journal.*` commands. Off, those commands only say so.

org_journal_dir.markdownDescription: The directory of the journal's files. `~/` is the home directory. (`org-journal-dir`)

org_journal_file_type.markdownDescription: A file a day (`daily`), week (`weekly`), month (`monthly`) or year (`yearly`); but daily, each entry has its date in a `CREATED` property. (`org-journal-file-type`)

org_journal_start_on_weekday.markdownDescription: The day a weekly file starts on: 1 is Monday, 7 Sunday. (`org-journal-start-on-weekday`)

org_journal_file_format.markdownDescription: The names of the files, as `format-time-string` writes the date their entries start on: with `%Y`, `%m` and `%d` (a yearly file needs only `%Y`, a monthly one `%Y` and `%m`). A name without `.org` is an Org file to org-journal, but not to most editors. (`org-journal-file-format`)

org_journal_date_format.markdownDescription: The date of an entry, after `org_journal_date_prefix`, as `format-time-string` writes it, in the C locale: `%x` is `10/09/26`. (`org-journal-date-format`)

org_journal_date_prefix.markdownDescription: What comes before the date of an entry: a headline, or `#+title: ` in a daily file. (`org-journal-date-prefix`)

org_journal_time_format.markdownDescription: The time of a new entry of the day, as `format-time-string` writes it; empty for none. (`org-journal-time-format`)

org_journal_time_format_post_midnight.markdownDescription: The time of an entry made after midnight while it is still yesterday (`org_extend_today_until`); empty for `org_journal_time_format`. (`org-journal-time-format-post-midnight`)

org_journal_time_prefix.markdownDescription: What comes before the time of an entry: its stars give its level. (`org-journal-time-prefix`)

org_journal_hide_entries_p.markdownDescription: Fold all but the new entry. (`org-journal-hide-entries-p`)

org_journal_carryover_items.markdownDescription: The items of the entry before that move to today's, with the headlines above them: a match of the tags view (`m`); empty for none. (`org-journal-carryover-items`)

org_journal_skip_carryover_drawers.markdownDescription: Drawers left out of the items carried over. (`org-journal-skip-carryover-drawers`)

org_journal_carryover_delete_empty_journ.markdownDescription: What happens to an entry or file left empty by the carryover: `never` deleted, `always`, or `ask`. (`org-journal-carryover-delete-empty-journal`)

org_journal_file_header.markdownDescription: What a new file starts with, as `format-time-string` writes it: `#+title: Journal %Y`. (`org-journal-file-header`)

org_journal_created_property_timestamp_f.markdownDescription: The date in the `CREATED` property of an entry of a file that is not daily. (`org-journal-created-property-timestamp-format`)

org_journal_scheduled_string.markdownDescription: What comes before the timestamp of an entry for a day to come (`org.journal.new.scheduled.entry`). (`org-journal-scheduled-string`)

org_journal_enable_encryption.markdownDescription: Tag the date of a new entry with `crypt`, for `org-crypt` to encrypt (`org.crypt.encrypt.all`, or as the file is saved with `org-crypt-use-before-save-magic` in the Emacs configuration). (`org-journal-enable-encryption`)

org_journal_enable_agenda_integration.markdownDescription: Add the journal's files of today and the days to come to the agenda's files. (`org-journal-enable-agenda-integration`)

org_journal_search_result_date_format.markdownDescription: The date of each result of a search of the journal, as `format-time-string` writes it. (`org-journal-search-result-date-format`)

org_journal_search_results_order_by.markdownDescription: The order of the results of a search of the journal: `asc`, the first day first, or `desc`, the last. (`org-journal-search-results-order-by`)

org_extend_today_until.markdownDescription: The hour before which it is still yesterday: for the agenda's today, the date prompt with nothing to start from, the times capture templates put in and the day of a datetree, `.+` and `++` repeaters, clock report ranges and org-journal's new entries. (`org-extend-today-until`)

org_agenda_search_view_always_boolean.markdownDescription: Read every search string of the search view (`s`) as words that must (`+word`, `word`) or must not (`-word`) occur, regexps in braces (`{regexp}`) and `"quoted phrases"`. Off, it is a phrase whose spaces match any whitespace, unless its first word starts with `+`, `-` or `{`. (`org-agenda-search-view-always-boolean`)

org_agenda_search_view_force_full_words.markdownDescription: The words of a Boolean search match whole words only, as a search string starting with `:` asks. (`org-agenda-search-view-force-full-words`)

org_agenda_search_view_max_outline_level.markdownDescription: The search view shows headlines down to this level, a match below one counting for the headline above: 0 for every level. (`org-agenda-search-view-max-outline-level`)

org_agenda_text_search_extra_files.markdownDescription: Files the search view (`s`) searches besides the agenda files, after them, as `org_agenda_files` names them. `agenda-archives` first adds the files the agenda files archive to. A file listed twice is searched at its last place. (`org-agenda-text-search-extra-files`)

org_agenda_prefix_format.markdownDescription: What comes before the headline on a line of the agenda (`agenda`), the TODO list (`todo`), tags searches (`tags`) and text searches (`search`): `%c` the category, `%t` the time, `%s` the leader (`Scheduled: `), `%e` the effort, `%l` a blank per level, `%T` the last tag, `%b` the headlines above (breadcrumbs), `%i` the icon (none). A width pads (`%-12c` on the right, `%12c` on the left), `.N` cuts, `%?` leaves out an empty field, and a character before the letter follows a value that is not empty (`%-12:c`). `%(…)` is Emacs Lisp, run by Emacs (the `emacs` option) on the entry's headline with `category`, `extra`, `level` … bound, as Org runs it: `%(org-entry-get nil "X")`, or a function of `emacs_config`. Without Emacs it is empty. (`org-agenda-prefix-format`)

org_agenda_todo_keyword_format.markdownDescription: How a TODO keyword is written in the agenda: `%-4s` pads it to four columns, so that the titles line up; an empty format leaves keywords out. (`org-agenda-todo-keyword-format`)

org_agenda_scheduled_leaders.markdownDescription: The leader of a scheduled entry on its day, and on today when its day has passed (`%d`: the days since). (`org-agenda-scheduled-leaders`)

org_agenda_deadline_leaders.markdownDescription: The leader of a deadline on its day, on today before it (`%d`: the days left), and on today after it (`%d`: the days since). (`org-agenda-deadline-leaders`)

org_agenda_deadline_faces.markdownDescription: The look of a deadline in the agenda by the part of its warning time that has passed: the first whose part is no more than that, none past the last. The faces are Org's: `org-imminent-deadline` (or `org-warning`), `org-upcoming-deadline`, `org-upcoming-distant-deadline`; any other name is the plain look. (`org-agenda-deadline-faces`)

org_agenda_timerange_leaders.markdownDescription: The leader of a time range within a day, and of a range over days (`%d`: which day of it, `%d`: how many days). (`org-agenda-timerange-leaders`)

org_agenda_inactive_leader.markdownDescription: What goes before an inactive timestamp's line, when the agenda shows them (`[`, `v [`). (`org-agenda-inactive-leader`)

org_agenda_remove_tags.markdownDescription: Leave the tags out of the agenda's lines; `prefix` only when the prefix shows a tag (`%T`). (`org-agenda-remove-tags`)

org_stuck_projects.markdownDescription: What the stuck projects view (`#`) lists: the projects the match string finds whose subtree has no entry with one of the TODO keywords (`*` for any not done) or tags (`*` for any), and no match of the regexp. (`org-stuck-projects`)

org_agenda_breadcrumbs_separator.markdownDescription: What goes between the headlines of `%b`. (`org-agenda-breadcrumbs-separator`)

org_agenda_format_date.markdownDescription: How the agenda writes a day, as `format-time-string` does: `%A %d %B %Y`, `%a %Y-%m-%d`. (`org-agenda-format-date`)

org_agenda_start_day.markdownDescription: The day the agenda starts from, as the date prompt reads it: `-1d`, `+2d`, `2026-10-01`. (`org-agenda-start-day`)

org_agenda_custom_commands_contexts.markdownDescription: Where the commands of `org_agenda_custom_commands` are offered, as for `org_capture_templates_contexts`. (`org-agenda-custom-commands-contexts`)

header.description: Replaces the view's header; empty for none

blocks.description: Views shown one after the other

match.description: For todo, keywords; for tags, a match string

header.description: Replaces the view's header; empty for none

settings.description: Agenda options for this block: org_agenda_span, org_agenda_start_day…

org_agenda_custom_commands.markdownDescription: Commands of the agenda menu. Each has a `key` and a `description`, and either a `type` (`agenda`, `alltodo`, `todo`, `tags` or `tags-todo`) with a `match` (keywords such as `NEXT|WAIT` for `todo`, a match string such as `work-home` or `PRIORITY="A"` for `tags`), or `blocks`, a list of such views shown one after the other. `header` replaces a view's header (empty: none), and `settings` holds agenda options for the command or a block (`org_agenda_span`, `org_agenda_start_day` …). A command with only a key and a description groups the commands whose keys start with its key. (`org-agenda-custom-commands`)
